rows.12:11038:
...You don't want to see it?
So you believe my story is true, {a}.
Thank you.
After all, you don't want to see it because it scares you, right?
Well, even if you'd wanted to see it, it would have been impossible.
Tokita dying at school caused quite a stir, but the dozens of films in the audiovisual room vanished without a trace, as if they had never existed at all.{p}
rows.12:11510:
The school on the screen had turned to night.
And on the screen, he himself was meeting a girl.
rows.12:11604:
(What if it's a videotape that shows the future?)
He'd watched too many movies too, hadn't he?
For an idea like that to pop into his head right away...
So he went to the school that night.{p}
rows.12:11820:
While Tokita was distracted by the breeze, a girl appeared at the spot that had been on the video.
(Huh? When did she get here?)
And without hesitation, Tokita walked toward her.
Then the girl said,
"Good evening."
Just like that, she spoke to him.
He felt as if he'd stepped into a movie.
"Come on, let's go."
That's what she said.
"Huh? Go where..."
"That's how it goes in the script, isn't it?"
He didn't want to lose the thrill of being inside a movie.
Tokita went along with her.{p}
rows.12:120c4:
You're going to stop editing?
I see. When someone involved in an amateur film has died, I can understand having second thoughts.
He'd finally founded the Film Research Society he'd longed for and gotten to the point of actually making a film, so he was bitterly disappointed too.
He was a warm-hearted person, so he decided to give up editing the film.
Besides, he was reluctant to edit a movie that showed a person who'd been murdered.{p}
rows.12:12340:
"The last time I was in the audiovisual room was last Saturday.
I'm sure I put all the editing equipment away then..."
After all, the only ones with keys to this room were the teacher and him...
And the teacher would hardly do something like that.
But he chose to look on the bright side.
Surely this was Katayama, who had met such a bitter end, pleading with him to finish the film...
There's no doubt he himself deeply regretted having to stop editing partway through.{p}
rows.12:12970:
"If you feel that strongly about it, then go ahead and quit."
Tokita agreed to let Nakayama quit.
Maybe Tokita cared far more about the film he was making right then than about that.
"Nakayama, would you help me with the editing, just for today?"
Tokita asked him.
It was his last day anyway, and he wanted to see the scenes he'd shot, so Nakayama decided to help.
They were both film lovers to begin with, after all.
I'm sure they enjoyed it, as you'd expect.{p}
rows.12:1312c:
There, the same thing Tokita had done to Nakayama was playing out.
I shut my eyes without thinking.
Even so, I could still hear Tokita's screams and the hissing of his face melting.
"Nakayama, please stop☆"
I cried out in spite of myself.{p}
rows.12:13478:
I see...
Well, I could make an exception and show it to you.
It must be fate that you and I met like this.
But I can't guarantee you'll come out of it alive.
Tokita was killed because he got involved with this film, after all.
Frankly, I think it's a more terrifying thing than anything edited into a finished movie.
Though you may not have thought so.
...I'll ask you once more.{p}You're saying you want to see the film I have?
rows.12:13640:
Anyone who believed my story couldn't normally give an answer like that...
I don't know what you're thinking, but if you insist that much, I'll show it to you.{p}
rows.12:136f4:
In exchange, there's one condition.
You'll come and see it alone with me.{p}Is that all right?
rows.12:137a8:
A hallway with the lights off is frightening, isn't it?
I wonder if the teacher on patrol has already gone home.
{a}.
From here on, whatever happens, there won't be any adults to help you.
Heh heh heh...
When people say someone is reckless with their life, I suppose they mean someone like you.{p}
rows.12:143c4:
...Practically chased out by Arai, I left the audiovisual room.
Only my footsteps echoed in the empty hallway.
That was a horrible story to hear.
I need to get back to the club room, fast.
I want this whole project over with, right now.
I wish I'd never said I wanted to see that tape...
But still... what's going on?
It feels like too many strange things are happening.
"Go back to the club room ahead of me."
They all say that to me.
Why on earth...?
At first, things were still fine.
Kazama's story was practically a joke.
I'd thought, huh, so this is all the school's seven wonders amount to...{p}
